title: Good Evidence, Bad Evidence
paragraphs: Father and Sakura-chan went to check out the shopping district. Apparently, they’re inspecting the local specialties and cuisine. Ren and Itsuki seemed somewhat excited—probably because it means we’ll have a feast tonight. Meanwhile, Ren and Yuki-chan are out surveying the surrounding areas. I don’t have everything mapped out myself, after all. There might be hunting grounds similar to the ones in the game. If we can obtain materials from monsters that only inhabit this region, we could enhance our abilities. Ren seemed eager about that. As for Itsuki, he’s exploring the town with Kou. They’re investigating the area while trying not to interact too much with the townspeople. Still, I can’t help but worry that they might get caught up in something. So, I decided to accompany Itsuki.
“At a glance, this just looks like a regular… town.”
“It does have a bit of a Chinese-style aesthetic to it, though.”
“That’s true. When this was just a game, it was based on a medieval setting, but there seem to be regional differences.”
“It appears so.”
“By the way, Motoyasu-san.”
“What is it?”

“Naofumi-san and Ren were also curious about this—there are some people among the townsfolk and adventurers who have distinctly Japanese-looking faces. And no one seems surprised by our presence. There must be a reason for that, right?”

Ah, that topic. I remember wondering about it from time to time when I was first summoned. Back then, I just assumed this world was a melting pot of different races and left it at that. But now, I know the answer.
“Itsuki, heroes are summoned to this world at a fairly regular rate. And after they make their mark, what usually happens to them?”
“They gain influence and are welcomed into powerful circles. And then… ah, I see. This is probably something Naofumi-san would react strongly to.”
Itsuki caught on and seemed to accept the explanation. Well, with that much of a hint, even he could figure it out.
“In other words, summoned heroes end up marrying and having children, which results in Japanese features appearing through genetic inheritance over generations.”
“That seems to be the case. But personally, I find it odd that only Japanese people are summoned so frequently.”
“Could it be that we just happened to be summoned as Japanese, and other foreigners have been summoned too?”
“I don’t know. I’ve gone through multiple loops, but I haven’t come across any records about that.”

The inscriptions found in the Spirit Tortoise’s country were written in Japanese. The documents in the land of the Phoenix were also in Japanese. I remember Father getting frustrated while reading what looked like someone’s personal journal.
“Even in the first world? Wait… Kou-san, please stop staring at my hair.”
“Why?”
“Because my hair is not your food.”
After scolding Kou, Itsuki turned to look at me. Was he referring to the first world?
“Back in the first world, I didn’t really participate in politics or investigations. All I cared about was the Filolials and world peace.”
“Isn’t that still the case?”

With a deep sigh, Itsuki exhaled. Well, he wasn’t wrong. I fight for true peace. Before, Father and the others handled these kinds of matters, but now, it’s my responsibility to take the initiative. After all, I’m the only one who can loop through time.
“At a glance, this town seems peaceful… but sometimes I wonder what kind of incidents are happening behind the scenes.”
“Isn’t it the same in Japan?”
“That’s a good point. Even if things look peaceful on the surface, there’s always something happening somewhere… there’s really no difference.”
“We’re not the police. If an incident unfolds right before our eyes, we have the strength to intervene a little, but our primary focus should be on the greater threat—the Waves.”

“That’s true… If we get too involved in local matters, we might end up being used, just like in Melromarc, where people pretended to be weak just to manipulate us. In the end, these things should be left to the ruling authorities.”

…It’s a difficult issue. I’ve seen my fair share of such situations. Unreasonable demands made under the weight of money, bounty hunters using brute force to take control of towns… In those cases, maybe stepping in forcefully wouldn’t be such a bad idea.
“Unlike game quests, there’s no predetermined ‘right’ answer. This really is another world, but at the same time, it’s reality.”
“Determining what’s ‘right’ is often a personal matter, but we still need to discern the best course of action.”

If Itsuki doesn’t find a way to release his pent-up frustration, his strong sense of justice might drive him to act recklessly. That reminded me—Father had warned him about this before. It would be good if he had some sort of outlet.
“Even when someone seems like an outright villain, we should still have the patience to hear them out,” Father had muttered after failing to convince Itsuki last time.

“…Listening to someone, even if they seem like a villain. You’re right. There’s that saying about not judging people by their appearance… If we dismiss their words as mere excuses without hearing them out, we’ll never uncover the truth.”
Was Itsuki a justice addict right after being summoned? Seeing him now, he sometimes comes up with rather unexpected insights.
“It’s complicated, but talking with Naofumi-san and Motoyasu-san has helped me understand things better.”
“Me and Father?”

“During this wagon journey, I’ve noticed that when Naofumi-san buys ingredients at shops, he first gauges the shopkeeper’s situation before negotiating a discount. You’ve noticed it too, right, Motoyasu-san?”
“Indeed. Father is a skilled negotiator.”
“What he’s doing is drawing out the seller’s limits through conversation. In a way, it’s similar to the relationship between justice and evil.”
That’s Itsuki’s take on things. Hearing Father get praised makes me feel good too.

“Naofumi-san wants to buy cheaply. The shop wants to sell at the highest possible price. If we frame this in terms of justice and evil, Naofumi-san represents the weak, trying to buy cheaply because he has no money, while the ‘evil’ side is the shop, profiting by selling at high prices…”
“That’s quite a forceful comparison.”

“Just hear me out. If we expand this idea, the weak can’t survive unless they buy things cheaply, while the strong—being the shop—sell at high prices, making it seem like they are squeezing the weak. If I were to stumble upon this without knowing any context, it would look like the shop is mercilessly exploiting the weak.”
“Hmm…?”
I’m not entirely sure where he’s going with this, but I nod along for now.

“But what if the shop also needs to sell at that price to survive? If I were to help the weak without knowing that fact and destroy the shop in the process, it would be no different from looting. That wouldn’t be justice at all. That’s why I need to understand the full picture.”
“So, you’re saying it’s important to learn the shop’s circumstances as well?”
“Exactly. Naofumi-san is skilled at negotiating in a way that ensures the shop isn’t at a loss while still getting a fair price.”
“But from what I heard, in the first world, you did gather information… yet still made mistakes, didn’t you?”

If Itsuki’s logic were flawless, then as long as he gathered information properly, he wouldn’t have made mistakes. And yet, he did. Why is that? Itsuki fell into deep thought once more in response to my question.
“Motoyasu-san, was there anything else Naofumi-san or the others warned me about in the first world?”
“I don’t really remember much…”
I have a vague sense that this is important information for keeping Itsuki from going off the rails. If I can give him good advice here, maybe he won’t lose control. So, I dig through my memories.

Did Father, Big Sister, or anyone else say anything back then? Or maybe the best answer is simply being honest about what I personally thought about Itsuki at the time. Ah, now that I think about it, I do recall Father and the others complaining… and I also remember my own thoughts on the matter.
“Rather than just gathering convenient evidence, wouldn’t it be better to also pay attention to inconvenient facts?”
Back then, when Father failed to convince Ren and Itsuki… I remember he said something similar about their strengthening methods.

“It’s just like with strengthening methods. You assume you’re right because you already ‘know’ something, and you don’t trust any other possibilities. So, even if another method exists, you immediately dismiss it as wrong. In a way, isn’t that also about justice and evil?”
“I-I see… If I only look for convenient evidence to prove something is wrong, I’ll end up fabricating a ‘truth’ that fits my own bias.”
Itsuki clapped his hands together, as if he had realized something.

“If I ignore the fact that a shop needs to sell at a certain price to survive and just rush to help those who appear weak, I accomplish nothing. Worse, if a so-called ‘weak person’ is actually struggling because they refused to work and were just being lazy, then I’d be turning a blind eye to that reality too.”
After nodding to himself several times, Itsuki looked back at the town.
“Gather as much information as possible, don’t ignore inconvenient truths, and then make a judgment… It was so much easier when this was just a game, but in reality, it’s so difficult.”
He’s talking about some complicated stuff.
“Well, as far as I’m concerned, if someone opposes me, it’s best to just beat some sense into them.”
